# Relevance labels for the federated ranking (v1-e08-t03)

For each search below, decide for each item whether you would want it in the first page of results
for a debater researching that query: **relevant** or **not relevant**. About 15 minutes for all
three. Items are in alphabetical order by title, which is neither the providers' order nor the
ranking's. Every item is invented (synthetic titles, authors and outlets), so judge it by its title
and summary as if it were real.

Reply with the item numbers you mark relevant for each search, for example `P02, P05, P09`. Every
item you do not list is recorded as not relevant. If a query's wording should be different for this
season's topic, say so too.

## Policy: "carbon border adjustment trade retaliation"

* **P01**: Border carbon adjustment design under WTO law. *Journal of International Economic Law Studies*, scholarly, 2022-06-01.
  Assesses whether a border carbon adjustment can be justified under GATT Article XX and which design choices invite legal challenge.
* **P02**: Carbon border adjustment mechanism. *Encyclopedia of Climate Policy Terms*, scholarly, 2023-01-01.
  (no summary)
* **P03**: Carbon border adjustments and the risk of trade retaliation: evidence from WTO disputes. *World Trade Review Letters*, scholarly, 2025-02-01.
  Across 41 trade disputes, border carbon adjustments raised the probability that partners exporting carbon-intensive goods imposed retaliatory tariffs within two years.
* **P04**: Carbon capture in cement production: a techno-economic review. *Journal of Cleaner Industry*, scholarly, 2024-03-01.
  Reviews 62 carbon capture pilots in cement kilns and estimates capture costs per tonne of CO2.
* **P05**: Carbon offsets market rebounds. *Example Markets*, news, 2026-10-18.
  Prices for voluntary carbon offsets rose for a third month as airlines bought credits.
* **P06**: Climate clubs and border adjustments: a game-theoretic analysis. *Environmental and Resource Economics Letters*, scholarly, 2020-05-01.
  Models when a border adjustment sustains a climate club and when it triggers a tariff war with non-members.
* **P07**: EU's carbon border levy enters full phase as India threatens countermeasures. *The Example Times*, news, 2026-10-15.
  India's commerce ministry said it would respond to the EU carbon border levy on steel with measures of its own.
* **P08**: Leakage and competitiveness effects of the EU carbon border adjustment mechanism. *Energy Policy Review*, scholarly, 2023-09-01.
  Simulates carbon leakage and export losses for steel, aluminium and cement under the EU mechanism and the responses of affected exporters.
* **P09**: Retaliation fears weigh on soybean farmers. *Example Farm Journal*, news, 2026-09-28.
  Growers worry new tariffs on farm machinery imports could prompt retaliation against soybeans.
* **P10**: Retaliation in the digital services tax disputes. *Tax Policy Quarterly*, scholarly, 2022-11-01.
  Traces threatened tariff retaliation against digital services taxes in six countries.
* **P11**: Steelmakers brace for carbon border costs. *Example Business*, news, 2026-10-02.
  Exporters to Europe expect certificate costs to cut margins and are lobbying for exemptions.
* **P12**: The political economy of carbon tariffs: exporter responses in India and China. *Global Environmental Politics Notes*, scholarly, 2024-08-01.
  Interviews with trade officials show both governments preparing countermeasures against carbon tariffs on steel and fertiliser.
* **P13**: Trade ministers meet ahead of G20. *Example Wire*, news, 2026-10-20.
  Ministers discussed supply chains, critical minerals and the WTO's dispute system.
* **P14**: Trade retaliation and the 2018-2019 tariff escalation. *Review of Trade Politics*, scholarly, 2021-04-01.
  Documents how retaliatory tariffs targeted politically salient agricultural exports during the 2018-2019 escalation.

## LD: "universal basic income labor force participation"

* **L01**: Basic income as a republican ideal of non-domination. *Political Philosophy Quarterly*, scholarly, 2018-09-01.
  Argues that an unconditional basic income secures freedom as non-domination by giving workers the power to refuse exploitative work.
* **L02**: Basic income bill stalls in state senate. *The Example Gazette*, news, 2026-10-19.
  The proposal would have paid every adult resident $500 a month; opponents cited work incentives.
* **L03**: City's guaranteed income pilot ends with mixed jobs data. *Example Metro*, news, 2026-10-10.
  Participants were more likely to find full-time work, but the effect faded after the payments stopped.
* **L04**: Guaranteed income pilots in U.S. cities: preliminary employment outcomes. *Urban Policy Working Papers*, scholarly, 2025-04-01.
  Across eleven city pilots, full-time employment rose slightly more among recipients than in control groups.
* **L05**: Income inequality and health: a review. *Public Health Reviews Digest*, scholarly, 2017-06-01.
  Reviews evidence linking income inequality to mortality and self-rated health.
* **L06**: Jobs report: participation rate ticks up to 62.9%. *Example Wire*, news, 2026-10-03.
  The labor force participation rate rose a tenth of a point as more prime-age women returned to work.
* **L07**: Labor force participation trends among prime-age men, 1970-2020. *Labor Statistics Review*, scholarly, 2021-03-01.
  Decomposes the fall in prime-age male participation into disability, education and regional factors.
* **L08**: Labor market participation of older workers in Japan. *Asian Labour Studies*, scholarly, 2016-11-01.
  Pension reform raised participation among workers aged 60 to 64.
* **L09**: Study: cash payments did not reduce work hours. *Example Daily*, news, 2026-10-12.
  Researchers found recipients of monthly payments worked about as many hours as the control group.
* **L10**: The Alaska Permanent Fund dividend and employment. *Applied Public Economics*, scholarly, 2020-02-01.
  The annual dividend had no effect on employment and raised part-time work.
* **L11**: Unconditional cash and work: a meta-analysis of 38 programs. *Journal of Social Policy Evidence*, scholarly, 2024-01-01.
  Pooled estimates show no significant reduction in labour force participation from unconditional cash transfers.
* **L12**: Universal basic income and labor supply: evidence from a Kenyan cash transfer experiment. *Development Economics Letters*, scholarly, 2023-07-01.
  Recipients of a 12-year unconditional transfer did not reduce hours worked and shifted from wage labour to self-employment.
* **L13**: Universal design for learning in higher education: a systematic review. *Higher Education Practice*, scholarly, 2019-10-01.
  Synthesizes 120 studies of universal design for learning in university courses.
* **L14**: Universal pre-K enrollment climbs. *Example Schools Report*, news, 2026-09-30.
  Enrollment in the state's universal pre-K program reached 71 percent of four-year-olds.

## PF: "nuclear power expansion grid reliability"

* **F01**: Capacity factors of the US nuclear fleet, 2000-2024. *Nuclear Operations Data*, scholarly, 2025-03-01.
  The fleet averaged a 92 percent capacity factor, the highest of any generation source.
* **F02**: Data center demand drives calls for new nuclear. *Example Tech*, news, 2026-10-05.
  Technology companies are seeking firm round-the-clock power and backing restarts of closed reactors.
* **F03**: Firm low-carbon generation and the cost of decarbonized grids. *Joule Letters Example*, scholarly, 2020-10-01.
  Grids with firm low-carbon power such as nuclear reach deep decarbonization at 10 to 62 percent lower cost.
* **F04**: Grid reliability under extreme heat: lessons from the 2021 Texas outage. *Energy Infrastructure Review*, scholarly, 2023-08-01.
  Attributes the outage to gas supply failures and unweatherized plants of every fuel type.
* **F05**: Nuclear magnetic resonance spectroscopy of battery electrolytes. *Electrochemistry Methods*, scholarly, 2022-05-01.
  Uses nuclear magnetic resonance to track electrolyte decomposition in lithium cells.
* **F06**: Nuclear power and grid reliability in high-renewable systems. *Power Systems Analysis*, scholarly, 2024-06-01.
  Firm nuclear capacity cut loss-of-load hours by two-thirds in modelled grids with 70 percent wind and solar.
* **F07**: Nuclear talks resume in Vienna. *Example Wire*, news, 2026-10-14.
  Diplomats returned to talks on enrichment limits and sanctions relief.
* **F08**: Power expansion in rural electrification programs. *Development Energy Notes*, scholarly, 2019-07-01.
  Evaluates mini-grid expansion in West African villages.
* **F09**: Public attitudes to nuclear power after Fukushima. *Energy and Society*, scholarly, 2016-02-01.
  Survey data from 24 countries show support for nuclear power fell and partly recovered by 2015.
* **F10**: Regulator warns of winter grid shortfall. *The Example Gazette*, news, 2026-10-08.
  The grid operator projected a reserve margin below target during a severe cold snap.
* **F11**: Small modular reactor cost overruns: a reference-class forecast. *Energy Economics Briefs*, scholarly, 2025-01-01.
  Historical megaproject overruns suggest first small modular reactors will cost twice their estimates and arrive years late.
* **F12**: Uranium prices hit 18-year high. *Example Markets*, news, 2026-10-21.
  Utilities signing long-term fuel contracts pushed spot uranium above $110 a pound.
* **F13**: Utility files plan for two new reactors citing reliability. *The Example Times*, news, 2026-10-16.
  The utility told regulators the reactors are needed to keep the grid reliable as coal plants retire.
